Axioma Style Factor Summary Axioma describes their style factors as follows: – Exchange-Rate Sensitivity – This is a measure of a stock's sensitivity to exchange rates as measured relative to a basket of currencies. Stocks with a positive Exchange-Rate Sensitivity score move in line with a basket of currencies, indicating that a larger proportion of business may come from non-domestic sources. – Growth – Growth gives an indication of a company's rate of growth historically. The growth factor is calculated as the product of one minus the dividend pay-out rate and the one-year return on equity. Stocks with a positive Growth score have recently experienced high growth levels as reflected by high retained earnings and high return on equity. – Leverage – Leverage provides a measure of a company's exposure to debt levels. This exposure is calculated as total debt divided by market capitalization. Total debt is the sum of long-term debt and debt in current liabilities (short-term debt). Stocks with a positive Leverage score have higher debt levels as a proportion of their stock market capitalization. LSEG Quantitative Analytics Database Schema for Axioma 16 – Liquidity – The liquidity factor provides a measure of a stock's trading activity, or lack thereof. The basic input is the last 20-day average volume divided by the last 20-day average market capitalization. Stocks with a positive Liquidity score are easier to trade in the market. – Market Sensitivity – This is a measure of a stock's under- or over-performance relative to the broad market from historical data. The basic input into this style is a traditional historical beta. Stocks with a positive Market Sensitivity score have larger historical betas. – Medium-Term Momentum – The Medium-Term Momentum gives a measure of a stock's past performance over the medium-term. It is defined as an asset's cumulative return over the last 300 trading days, excluding the last 20 trading days. Stocks with a positive Medium-Term Momentum score have outperformed over the past 13 months (excluding last month). – Short-Term Momentum – Short-Term Momentum gives a measure of a stock's recent performance. It is defined as an asset's cumulative return over the last 20 trading days. Stocks with a positive Short-Term Momentum score have outperformed over the past month. – Size – Differentiation of stocks based on market capitalization (for example, large and small stocks). It is defined using the market capitalization, averaged over the last 20 trading days. Market capitalization is computed as the product of the total shares outstanding and the unadjusted closing price on each day. Stocks with a positive Size score are larger capitalization stocks. – Value – Value gives a measure of how fairly a stock is priced within the market. The Value factor is calculated as the ratio of common equity to the current market capitalization (Book-to-Price). Stocks with a positive Value score have a high Book-to-Price and are viewed as relatively inexpensive as compared to their book value. – Volatility – Volatility gives a measure of an asset's relative volatility over time according to its historical behavior. The basic input into this style is an asset's absolute return averaged over the last 60 days divided by the cross-sectional volatility of the market. Stocks with a positive Volatility score have had very high or very low returns over the past quarter.

For LSEG Quantitative Analytics self-sourced data (where [table name].ExchCode = 0), this field defines the entity or event observing the special date. For other data, Name describes the holiday observed on the given date. For an illustration of how to interpret the data in this field, see Create Joins to Return Descriptions of Special Dates on page 20. Examples: Special Dates Tables Create Joins to Return ExchCode for Datastream's ExchIntCode The ExchIntCode from the Datastream table Ds2Exchange can be mapped to ExchCode using the Ds2XRef table. Use the following query to get the ExchCode for an ExchIntCode. Example 1 SELECT A.ExchIntCode, A.ExchName, B.Desc_, C.* FROM Ds2Exchange A LEFT JOIN Ds2XRef B ON B.Code=A.ExchIntCode AND B.Type_=1017 LEFT JOIN SDExchInfo_V C ON C.ExchCode=B.Desc_ Create Joins to Return Descriptions of Special Dates These sample queries join SDInfo_v and SDDates_v to return the special date description for a given date and code. Example 2 This query returns the name of the entity observing the special date (under Name) where the Code is 34, the Date_ is December 12, 2001, and the ExchCode is 0. SELECT * FROM SDINFO_V A JOIN SDDATES_V B ON A.CODE=B.CODE LSEG Quantitative Analytics Database Schema for Core Tables 21 WHERE A.CODE=34 AND B.DATE_='2001-12-12' AND B.EXCHCODE=0 Code Name Code Date_ ExchCode 34 Exchange Holidays – Mexico 34 2001-12-12 00:00:00.000 0 Example 3 This query returns the name of the holiday (under Name) where the ExchCode is 371 and the Date_ is December 12, 2019. description: DNSIndicator is the DNS (Data Explorers Negative Sentiment) indicator. It is based on the normalized sum of the moving average of utilization and the change in utilization. This indicator is based on a relative scale (normalized) from 0 to 100. A relatively high DNS generally reflects negative sentiment (an increasing amount of shorts relative to longs), while a low number shows relatively less negative sentiment.

filename: QA Database Schema - Data Explorers v1.0.4 (2022-02-22).pdf
description: DIPSIndicator is the DIPS (Data Explorers Increasing Price Squeeze) indicator. It compares security-lending data (change in inventory quantity and loans) to cash market data (average trade volume and close price) to determine the risk of a rapid increase in price (price squeeze). DIPSIndicator gives a higher score to stocks that have a high level of utilization, a high loan position relative to cash market volume, a high proportion of shares outstanding on loan, a recent sharp declines in stock price, and a falling inventory that is available to borrow. The indicator is based on a relative scale from 0 to 100.

filename: QA Database Schema - Data Explorers v1.0.4 (2022-02-22).pdf
description: DIMVIndicator is the DIMV (Data Explorers Increasing Market Volatility) indicator. It combines the DNS and DIPS indicators. If only one of these indicators has a high value, or if the combination of the two results in a high value, then there is a higher risk of stock price volatility. The indicator is based on a relative scale from 0 to 100.

filename: QA Database Schema - Data Explorers v1.0.4 (2022-02-22).pdf
description: DPSIndicator is the DPS (Data Explorers Positive Sentiment) indicator. It is based on the average loan quantity (shorts) relative to the average inventory quantity (longs) for the security, with a higher score for stocks that have had little or no shorting activity over the previous 12 months. This indicator is based on a relative scale (normalized) from 0 to 100. A relatively high DPS generally reflects positive sentiment (relatively more longs than shorts), while a relatively low number shows negative sentiment.

filename: QA Database Schema - Data Explorers v1.0.4 (2022-02-22).pdf

CAP Capital repayment A capital repayment is different from a capital event because it comes from the share premium account, not issued capital. CPL Long term capital gains payment This indicates a long-term capital gains payment, paid from capital gains accrued by the company. CPM Mid term capital gains payment This indicates a medium-term capital gains payment, paid from capital gains accrued by the company. CPS Short term capital gains payment This indicates a short-term capital gains payment, paid from capital gains accrued by the company. CPU Undefined capital gains payment This indicates an undefined capital gains payment, paid from capital gains accrued by the company. This is the equivalent of CPG. FIN Final FIN indicates a final payment. FOR Forecast Dividend HYR Half yearly This indicates a regular half-yearly payment with a frequency of two per year. The standard Asset4 to Core Table mapping using ventype=46 (ASSET4) is based on one to one mapping logic from organization to a single security. This architecture limits from mapping companies with multiple listings across regions (Global and North America) and multiple issues (share classes A, B, C etc.) linking with Asset4 content set to obtain the corresponding ESG data. description: Category code is to distinguish the contribution type of activities as enabling or transitional. The terms "enabling" and "transitional" refer to different types of economic activities based on their contribution to environmental objectives. Enabling activities are those that provide goods, services, or technologies that help other economic activities to reduce their environmental impact. These activities are important for promoting the transition to a more sustainable economy by creating new markets and business models that support environmental objectives. For example, an enabling activity could be the production of renewable energy equipment, which helps enable the transition to a low-carbon energy system. Transitional activities, on the other hand, are those that directly contribute to environmental objectives by reducing greenhouse gas emissions or other environmental impacts. These activities are necessary for achieving the EU's climate and environmental objectives, such as the goal of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. Examples of transitional activities include the development and deployment of renewable energy technologies, energy-efficient buildings, and sustainable transport systems."

description: Corporate Flag reflects 1 if the segment division comprises of unallocated items or corporate assets primarily related to the company headquarters and head office expenses. Corporate segment consists of financing costs, working capital balances and cost allocated to common support functions which are not directly accountable to operating segments. description: Other Flag reflects 1 if the segment division comprises of miscellaneous or a combination of items aggregated in a single segment. Other segment includes an aggregate of items with nominal or insignificant activities clubbed in the operating segment. The flag is available for Business, Geographic, Product and Customer segment. Calculation of segment ratios generally exclude Other segment and NAICS codes will not be assigned. Other segment is considered as generic segment if the company is silent or indicates that it consists of common income and expenses, as referred in the example below. Segment note: Operating segments reported consists of water business comprising regulated water and wastewater treatment; non- household water relates to retail market and other segment include company financing arrangement and taxation. Water and Non-household segment are considered as operating segment, while Other is flagged a 1 since it is miscellaneous.

description: Segment Name is a textual column to capture the as-reported segment name disclosed by the company. In few exceptional cases the segment names may be different from the as-reported description to provide more meaningful names, as in case of abbreviations. description: Standardized Currency ID is the currency used for standardization of financials on product views. In majority of the cases the standardized replicates the as-reported currency disclosed by the company. But there are few rare cases where they differ as in the below scenarios: where the local currency relates to a country with a hyperinflationary economy and historical values rapidly become meaningless. In this case the standardized currency would be set as the global substitute currency used within that country. European Union countries officially switched Euro, but if few companies continue to disclose in the local or heritage currency the same will be converted to Euro on product to help comparability. When a country switches to new currency, historic data will be converted to reflect the global standardized currency of the country. When a company reports its financial data in more than one currency; for example, the main financials of the company are in USD, but few key operating metrics data is reported in Euro, standardization converts the minor data and displays based on the global currency assigned for the company. The Standardized Currency ID reflects in 3 alphabets based on the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) guidelines. Example: EUR- Euro, USD- US Dollar.

description: Cumulative Type Code is associated with the financial data collected for a particular period and appropriate code is assigned based on the periodic data collected. Interim reports disclose quarterly and half-yearly information for a semi-annual period. For a quarterly report 3 months data and for semi-annual 6 months data is marked as D -Discrete type. Discrete type is applicable for income statement and cash flow statements. Interim reports also disclose both quarterly and year-to-date (YTD) information. For a quarterly report 3, 6, 9 and 12 months year to data or cumulative data is marked as Y-Year to Date. Year-to-date information is applicable for income statement and cash flow statements. Cumulative Type Code consists of 4 codes: B - Both, implies that the period is first quarter of the fiscal year which is both Discrete and Year to date, D - Discrete, implies the quarterly 3 months info or 6 months for semi-annual, Y - Year to Date, implies quarterly cumulative data for 6, 9 and 12 months and N - Not Applicable, applicable for balance sheet statement as it is assessed as on the period end date. The below example illustrates the Cumulative Type Code used for interim periods based on the period length and interim period. – Period End Date - 6/30/2020, Period Length - 3, Period Length Unit Code - M, Periodicity Code -Q, Interim period- 1, Cumulative Type Code - B; – Period End Date - 9/30/2020, Period Length - 6, Period Length Unit Code - M, Periodicity Code - Q, Interim period- 2, Cumulative Type Code - Y; – Period End Date - 9/30/2020, Period Length - 3, Period Length Unit Code - M, Periodicity Code - Q, Interim period- 2, Cumulative Type Code – D; – Period End Date - 9/30/2020, Period Length - 0, Period Length Unit Code - M, Periodicity Code - Q, Interim period- 2, Cumulative Type Code - N.

description: Credit Flag is associated with the sign or polarity of the amount or value collected for the financial information. Each data item has default polarity based on the nature of the data items. Generally, items related to income/gain are assigned positive, and expense/loss are assigned negative. Credit Flag reflects 1 if the default polarity of the data item is positive and 0 if negative. In the below illustration, the financial data items represented by the Financial Concept Code and description are marked with 1 if defaulted as positive and 0 if negative: Financial Concept Code - ACAE, Financial Concept Description - Cash and Cash Equivalents, Credit Flag- 1.

description: Currency ID is the currency used for standardization of financials on product views. In majority of the cases the standardized replicates the as-reported currency disclosed by the company. But there are few rare cases where they differ as in the below scenarios: where the local currency relates to a country with a hyperinflationary economy and historical values rapidly become meaningless. In this case the standardized currency would be set as the global substitute currency used within that country. European Union countries officially switched Euro, but if few companies continue to disclose in the local or heritage currency the same will be converted to Euro on product to help comparability. When a country switches to new currency, historic data will be converted to reflect the global standardized currency of the country. When a company reports its financial data in more than one currency; for example, the main financials of the company are in USD, but few key operating metrics data is reported in Euro. Standardization converts the minor data and displays based on the global currency assigned for the company. Currency ID reflects in 3 alphabets based on the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) guidelines EUR, USD, JPY.

description: Estimated Flag is associated with the financial data items calculated using the standardized data and is marked 1 if one of the inputs is an estimated value. Estimated Flag indicates the estimated attribute of the analytical value, the flag is marked 1 if one of the inputs used in the calculation of the analytics comes directly or indirectly from an estimated data. It is marked 0 if the input is an as-reported value.

description: Instance Key is associated with the financial data values derived or calculated by the system using the as-reported content. Analytical data value may be derived either through summation, deduction, multiplication, or division using as-reported values to provide meaningful ratios, and each value is assigned an Instance Key. Each analytical value is assigned with a unique identifier known as Instance Key. The below example illustrates the Instance Key assigned to each analytic value: Organization ID - 4295856044, Period ID - 1, Analytic Concept Code - SCAES, Code description - Cash and Short-Term Investments - Total per Share, Analytic Value - 1.054038005, Instance Key - 6516460032.

For example: Business, Geographic, Customer and Product type, except for Eliminations, Corporate and Other which are generic segments. Each segment name is assigned with a numerical value or Segment ID in a chronological order across segment types to avoid duplicate names. description: Segment Line Item ID is associated with the segment display on the standardized layer and is applicable to Business, Geographic, Customer and Product sections. Segment Line Item ID helps to display the items in an orderly manner across all company to ease comparison.

filename: QA Database Schema - EU Taxonomy v1.1 (2025-07-08).pdf
description: Financial Concept Code is associated with the collection of each financial data item on the product and each code is unique assigned to each accounting concept. Financial Concept Codes are chart of accounts with the list of common accounting concepts available in the taxonomy. There are two layers of Financial Concept Code displayed; one is the as- reported layer, and another is standardized layer. Standardized Financial Concept Code is generally the aggregate of the as-reported codes based on the nature of items. Standardization helps comparability across all markets and GAAP reporting. In the below illustration, the Standardized Financial Concept Code SINY-Inventories Total is the aggregate of all the granular components such as raw material, finished goods, tools and fixtures, work-in-progress, and others: Financial Concept Code - SINY, Financial Concept Code Description - Inventories Total.

filename: QA Database Schema - EU Taxonomy v1.1 (2025-07-08).pdf
description: Standardized Value is associated with the amount of each financial data item calculated with the aggregation of the as-reported items. Standardization helps comparability across all markets and GAAP reporting. Standardized Value is an aggregate of the components, calculated based on the nature of item irrespective of the reporting pattern.

filename: QA Database Schema - EU Taxonomy v1.1 (2025-07-08).pdf
description: Total Flag is associated with the segments applicable to Business, Geographic, Customer and Product sections. The as-reported segment values are aggregated to provide comparable data across all companies. For example, a banking company may disclose components of revenues such as interest income, investment income, realized gain/loss on investments and dividend income in its business segment note. The aggregate of revenue is calculated, and the total value is derived. Total Flag is marked as 1 when the value is an aggregate based on the as-reported components.

description: The average annualized earnings per share growth for a company over the past five years. The average annualized growth in EPS for the past five years is calculated by measuring the slope of a least squares curve fit to the logarithm of the reported earnings (a log- linear curve) and is expressed as a percent. If quarterly data are available, the line is fit to the last 21 observations (minimum of 11 observations) of rolling four quarter EPS. The resultant slope is multiplied by four and exponentialized to obtain an annualized growth factor. If semi-annual data are available, the curve is fit to the last 11 (minimum of 6) observations of these semi-annual data. The resultant slope is multiplied by two and exponentialized to obtain an annualized growth factor. If only annual observations are available, the curve is fit to the last 6 annual (minimum of 3) observations (5 time periods) and the exponentiated slope is used to represent the growth factor. Zero and negative observations are excluded from the calculations.

LSEG Financials and LSEG Financials PIT Lookup Tables The lookup tables contain integer and character code translations. These tables are shared between the LSEG Financials and LSEG Financials Point in Time (PIT) schemas. PK Type_ PK Code PK Type_ PK Code Lookup table data is divided according to whether the referenced code is integer-based or character-based. Integer-based codes are translated in RKDFndCode, and character-based codes are translated in RKDFndDesc. In some cases, you may need to translate data between the tables. For example, for the table RKDFndCmpRef, currency codes are referenced as integers. In this case, you use RKDFndCode to translate the integer code into the three-character ISO currency code. You can then use RKDFndDesc to translate the ISO currency code into the common currency name. In both cases the referenced code maps to the same lookup table value, which for currency codes is Type_ = 58. To translate the currency code in one step, you can use this query: select a.type_, a.code, a.desc_, b.desc_ from rkdfndcode a left join rkdfnddesc b on a.type_ = b.type_ and a.desc_ = b.code where b.type_ = 58 order by code You can modify this code sample to work with other Type_ values as needed.

SQL Views The SQL Views provide simplified calls that run complex SQL code and address key data nuances and mapping requests in the LSEG Quantitative Analytics database, making it much easier to access data through LSEG Quantitative Analytics. The RQA Support Team is available to provide training on the library structure and how to use the SQL Views. Contact Get Support if you would like the SQL views added to your server. Multiple securities under the same company mostly have the same set of fundamental data and RepNo. At the same time, it is possible for securities listed in different countries to follow different accounting standards. Therefore, the same company may be required to provide separate filings under different RepNo. RKD PIT tries to limit the number of RepNo with fundamental data under the same company. This view shows the best mapping practices when mapping QAID to RKDPIT. Index Fields ID, SecCode, Typ, Rank, RKD_Code, MapType

description: TableName is the name of the table where the data item is stored. Relationship Between MS2Item and MS2ItemMap Use MS2ItemMap to determine the table in which a particular data item from MS2Item is stored. Each MSCI version 2 data item is stored in one or more tables. The location of a specific data item depends on whether it is index- or security-level, the data type, how often it is updated (daily or monthly), and whether it is Advanced Corporate Event (ACE) data. The names of the MSCI version 2 data tables reflect the the type of data items they contain. The table name format is MS2[Idx|Sec][Datatype][Frq][ACE]. For details about this table name format, see Table Name Format on page 6. The following query returns the full mapping of the MSCI version 2 data items and corresponding data tables. select i.Item, i.Mnemonic, i.Desc_, i.AdjCode, i.ParentItem, i.DataTypeCode, i.DecimalNum, i.BoxFlg, i.DSFlg, i.BasicFlg, i.EnhFlg, i.LegacyMnem, m.SecFlg, m.IdxFlg, m.FrqFlg, m.DlyFlg, m.MthFlg, m.ACEFlg, m.TableName from MS2Item i join MS2ItemMap m on m.DataTypeCode = i.DataTypeCode and ((m.SecFlg = i.SecFlg) or (m.IdxFlg = i.IdxFlg)) -- AN ITEM MAY BE SECURITY LEVEL, INDEX LEVEL OR BOTH and ((m.MthFlg = i.MthFlg) or (m.DlyFlg = i.DlyFlg and m.FrqFlg = i.FrqFlg)) -- AN ITEM MAY BE MONTHLY OR DAILY. description: LicFlag describes licensing requirements: – LicFlag = 1 for UK and Canada – LicFlag = 2 for Asia LSEG Quantitative Analytics Database Schema for Ownership and Global Insider 32 8. Ownership Schema: This section includes sample queries demonstrating how to return all securities by the same issuer, and how to use an owner ID to return the holdings of the owner on a given date. These examples reference the TRQA core master tables. For more information about the master tables, see the Database Schema for LSEG Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document, available on the LSEG Quantitative Analytics product page on MyAccount. Example 1: Securities by Issuer This query takes a given domestic ID and returns all securities linked to the given ID by the same Issuer. DECLARE @ID VARCHAR(20) SET @ID = 'IBM' -- IBM SELECT T.VENNAME , S2.ID , O.ISSUERNAME , I2.SECNAME , I2.CUSIP , D.DESC_ AS SECURITY_CLASS FROM QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMSTRX S JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMAPX M ON M.SECCODE = S.SECCODE AND M.VENTYPE = 21 AND M.RANK = 1 JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNSECINFO I ON I.SECURITYCODE = M.VENCODE JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNSECISSUER O ON O.ISSUERCODE = I.ISSUERCODE JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNSECINFO I2 ON I2.ISSUERCODE = I.ISSUERCODE JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMAPX M2 ON M2.VENCODE = I2.SECURITYCODE AND M2.VENTYPE = 21 JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECVENTYPE T ON M.VENTYPE = T.VENTYPE LSEG Quantitative Analytics Database Schema for Ownership and Global Insider 33 JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMSTRX S2 ON S2.SECCODE = M2.SECCODE AND S2.TYPE_ = 1 LEFT JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNDESC D ON D.CODE = I2.SECCLSCODE AND D.TYPE_ = 5 -- Security Class Description WHERE S.ID = @ID Example 2: Holdings by Owner This query uses an owner ID and a date to return the holdings of the given owner on the given date. The query links to the TRQA core master tables, SECMSTRX and GSECMSTRX, to return the TRQA ID for each holding of the owner. DECLARE @OWNER INT DECLARE @DATE SMALLDATETIME SET @OWNER = 22006187 -- Berkshire Hathaway SET @DATE = '2008-06-30' SELECT T.VENNAME , O.OWNERCODE , O.OWNERNAME , H.QTRDATE , H.REPORTDATE , ISNULL(S.ID, S2.ID) AS ID , ISNULL(S.NAME, S2.NAME) AS NAME , ISNULL(S.CUSIP, S2.SEDOL) AS CUSIP_OR_SEDOL , H.SHARESHELD , H.VALUEHELD , H.SHARESCHG , H.VALUECHG FROM QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNINFO O JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNHOLDDET H ON H.OWNERCODE = O.OWNERCODE AND H.QTRDATE = @DATE AND H.REPORTDATE =( SELECT MAX(REPORTDATE) FROM QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNHOLDDET WHERE OWNERCODE = H.OWNERCODE AND SECURITYCODE = H.SECURITYCODE ) JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNSECINFO I ON I.SECURITYCODE = H.SECURITYCODE LEFT JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMAPX M LSEG Quantitative Analytics Database Schema for Ownership and Global Insider 34 ON M.VENCODE = I.SECURITYCODE AND M.VENTYPE = 21 LEFT JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECVENTYPE T ON M.VENTYPE = T.VENTYPE LEFT JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMSTRX S ON S.SECCODE = M.SECCODE AND S.TYPE_ = 1 LEFT JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.GSECMAPX M2 ON M2.VENCODE = I.SECURITYCODE AND M2.VENTYPE = 21 LEFT JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.GSECMSTRX S2 ON S2.SECCODE = M2.SECCODE WHERE O.OWNERCODE = @OWNER ORDER BY VALUEHELD DESC Example 3: Funds and Holdings This query shows how to see a company, the funds it operates, and the holdings of one of its funds. --1) Name of the Asset Management (Fund) house: select * from owninfo where ownercode = 22027248 --2) Funds managed by the “Macquarie” as a Asset Manager. select a.ownercode, a.ownername, a.address1, a.address2, a.city, a.url, a.p_ownercode, a.statuscode, a.orientcode, a.ownstylecode, d.Desc_ as OwnStyleDesc, a.owntypecode, b.Desc_ as OwnTypeDesc from OwnInfo a left join OwnCode b on b.code = a.owntypecode and b.type_ = 16 left join Owncode d on d.code = a.ownstylecode and d.type_ = 18 where a.p_ownercode = 22027248 order by ownername --3) Holdings of the particular fund from Macq. Asset Family: LSEG Quantitative Analytics Database Schema for Ownership and Global Insider 35 DECLARE @OWNER INT DECLARE @DATE SMALLDATETIME SET @OWNER = 22503079 -- Ownercode of one of the Funds held in #2 SET @DATE = '2010-12-31' SELECT T.VENNAME , O.OWNERCODE , O.OWNERNAME , H.QTRDATE , H.REPORTDATE , ISNULL(S.ID, S2.ID) AS ID , ISNULL(S.NAME, S2.NAME) AS NAME , ISNULL(S.CUSIP, S2.SEDOL) AS CUSIP_OR_SEDOL , H.SHARESHELD , H.VALUEHELD , H.SHARESCHG , H.VALUECHG FROM QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNINFO O JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNHOLDDET H ON H.OWNERCODE = O.OWNERCODE AND H.QTRDATE = @DATE AND H.REPORTDATE =( SELECT MAX(REPORTDATE) FROM QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNHOLDDET WHERE OWNERCODE = H.OWNERCODE AND SECURITYCODE = H.SECURITYCODE ) JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNSECINFO I ON I.SECURITYCODE = H.SECURITYCODE LEFT JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMAPX M ON M.VENCODE = I.SECURITYCODE AND M.VENTYPE = 21 LEFT JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECVENTYPE T ON M.VENTYPE = T.VENTYPE LEFT JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMSTRX S ON S.SECCODE = M.SECCODE AND S.TYPE_ = 1 LEFT JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.GSECMAPX M2 ON M2.VENCODE = I.SECURITYCODE AND M2.VENTYPE = 21 LEFT JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.GSECMSTRX S2 ON S2.SECCODE = M2.SECCODE LSEG Quantitative Analytics Database Schema for Ownership and Global Insider 36 WHERE O.OWNERCODE = @OWNER ORDER BY VALUEHELD DESC --4) Contact info of the Fund Manager: select * from owncon a join ownconinfo b on a.contactcode = b.contactcode where a.ownercode = '22503079' Example 4: Snapshot of Owners of a Security This query returns a snapshot of the owners of a particular security. DECLARE @DATE SMALLDATETIME SET @DATE = '8/17/09' ; WITH OWNDATA AS ( ROW_NUMBER () OVER (PARTITION BY H.OWNERCODE, H.SECURITYCODE ORDER BY REPORTDATE DESC) AS ROW , T.VENNAME , M.ID , M.CUSIP , O.OWNERCODE , O.OWNERNAME , H.QTRDATE , H.REPORTDATE , H.SHARESHELD , O.STATUSCODE , H.FLGSRCCODE , D.DESC_ AS RPT_SOURCE QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNINFO O JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNHOLDDET H ON H.OWNERCODE = O.OWNERCODE JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNCODE D ON H.FLGSRCCODE = D.CODE AND D.TYPE_ = 11 LSEG Quantitative Analytics Database Schema for Ownership and Global Insider 37 JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMAPX P ON P.VENCODE = H.SECURITYCODE AND P.VENTYPE = 21 JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECVENTYPE T ON P.VENTYPE = T.VENTYPE JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMSTRX M ON M.SECCODE = P.SECCODE AND M.TYPE_ = 1 WHERE H.SECURITYCODE = 25660 -- IBM AND H.HLDGTYPE = 1 -- INSTITUTIONS HOLDINGS AND QTRDATE = '3/31/09' AND STATUSCODE = 'Y' -- OWNER IS CURRENTLY TRACKED AND RESEARCHED (N = OWNER IS NOT TRACKED) AND H.FLGSRCCODE IN (1,6,499,503) -- REPORTING SOURCE ) SELECT * FROM OWNDATA WHERE ROW = 1 AND SHARESHELD > 0 ORDER BY REPORTDATE , OWNERNAME LSEG Quantitative Analytics Database Schema for Ownership and Global Insider Copyright © 2024 London Stock Exchange Group plc and its group of companies (LSEG) and/or its affiliates. description: For non-debt issues, if an issue asset/instrument has at least one quote that is active (AssetState = 'AC'), then AssetState is Active 'AC'. If all quote assets are deactivated (AssetState = 'DC'), then AssetState is Deactivated 'DC'. AssetState is derived for all asset types except debt issues that are maintained by the DBS forward feed. AssetState is 'NA' (Not Applicable) when no quote asset is found against the issue/instrument. In particular, new issues get 'NA' status as soon as they are created and until a quote is assigned to them. NA also applies to instruments not properly classified. States other than AC, DC, and NA are only set for fixed income issues. The full set of states is: – "CA" = "Called" – "DE" = "Defaulted" – "EX" = "Exchanged" – "ME" = "Merged" – "MA" = "Matured" – "RE" = "Redenominated" – "AC" = "Active" – "DC" = "De-activated" – "NA" = "Not applicable"

description: For non-debt issues, if an issue asset/instrument has at least one quote that is active (AssetState = 'AC'), then AssetState is Active 'AC'. If all quote assets are deactivated (AssetState = 'DC'), then AssetState is Deactivated 'DC'. AssetState is derived for all asset types except debt issues that are maintained by the DBS forward feed. AssetState is 'NA' (Not Applicable) when no quote asset is found against the issue/instrument. In particular, new issues get 'NA' status as soon as they are created and until a quote is assigned to them. NA also applies to instruments not properly classified. States other than AC, DC, and NA are only set for fixed income issues. The full set of states is: – "CA" = "Called" – "DE" = "Defaulted" – "EX" = "Exchanged" – "ME" = "Merged" – "MA" = "Matured" – "RE" = "Redenominated" – "AC" = "Active" – "DC" = "De-activated" – "NA" = "Not applicable"

description: For non-debt issues, if an issue asset/instrument has at least one quote that is active (AssetState = 'AC'), then AssetState is Active 'AC'. If all quote assets are deactivated (AssetState = 'DC'), then AssetState is Deactivated 'DC'. AssetState is derived for all asset types except debt issues that are maintained by the DBS forward feed. AssetState is 'NA' (Not Applicable) when no quote asset is found against the issue/instrument. In particular, new issues get 'NA' status as soon as they are created and until a quote is assigned to them. NA also applies to instruments not properly classified. States other than AC, DC, and NA are only set for fixed income issues. The full set of states is: – "CA" = "Called" – "DE" = "Defaulted" – "EX" = "Exchanged" – "ME" = "Merged" – "MA" = "Matured" – "RE" = "Redenominated" – "AC" = "Active" – "DC" = "De-activated" – "NA" = "Not applicable"

description: PermRegion is the permission region. There are multiple ARM, EQ, and IV regions that fit into a single permission Database Schema for Starmine Data 12 3. StarMine Regional Data Model Tables StarMine data is organized first by data model, and then by region. Availability of data depends on your data license. Data Models The StarMine data models are: – ARM (Analyst Revision Models): table names begin with Sm2DArm* – CRM (Credit Risk Models): table names begin with Sm2DCRM* – EQ (Earnings Quality): table names begin with Sm2DEq* – IV (Intrinsic Value): table names begin with Sm2DIv* – Smart Holdings: table names begin with Sm2DSH* – Val-Mo (Value Momentum) and Price-Mo (Price Momentum): table names begin with Sm2DVMo*. The Val-Mo model combines the StarMine ARM and IV Regional Models with the Price-Mo factor. NOTE. To access Daily Val-Mo Model data you must be licensed for StarMine ARM and IV daily regional Models. The Daily Val- Mo model license includes Price-Mo Daily data; however, Price- Mo may also be licensed separately. Regional Data Categories StarMine regional data is divided into these categories: – Americas: table names end in *AM – Asia Pacific: table names end in *AP – Europe, Middle East, and Africa: table names end in *EA Regional tables are organized identically and differ only by name and content. For this reason, regional tables share common descriptions. For example, the description for Sm2DArm* applies to the regional ARM tables Sm2DArmAM, Sm2DArmAP, and Sm2DArmEA. Regional Daily Data Adjustments Regional data is updated daily, and the data is unadjusted. StarMine Daily data is provided "as was," so it is not adjusted for any corporate actions. Any historical data items which require split adjustments are applied by StarMine and are refreshed with each monthly update. description: For non-debt issues, if an issue asset/instrument has at least one quote that is active (AssetState = 'AC'), then AssetState is Active 'AC'. If all quote assets are deactivated (AssetState = 'DC'), then AssetState is Deactivated 'DC'. AssetState is derived for all asset types except debt issues that are maintained by the DBS forward feed. AssetState is 'NA' (Not Applicable) when no quote asset is found against the issue/instrument. In particular, new issues get 'NA' status as soon as they are created and until a quote is assigned to them. NA also applies to instruments not properly classified. States other than AC, DC, and NA are only set for fixed income issues. The full set of states is: – "CA" = "Called" – "DE" = "Defaulted" – "EX" = "Exchanged" – "ME" = "Merged" – "MA" = "Matured" – "RE" = "Redenominated" – "AC" = "Active" – "DC" = "De-activated" – "NA" = "Not applicable"
